title.zh: 給免疫細胞裝上「自動斷電開關」：CAR-T療法的新曙光
title.en: Installing an 'Auto-Shutoff' Switch for Immune Cells: The New Dawn of CAR-T Therapy

summary.zh:
【總結】加州大學斯坦福大學團隊在《Cell》發表突破性研究，開發出名為「活化誘導釋放」（Activation-Induced Release, AIR）的基因開關技術。這項技術利用人體內的ADAM17蛋白酶，為免疫細胞（特別是CAR-T細胞）賦予了自主調節表面受體強度的能力。這不僅解決了CAR-T療法中常見的細胞疲勞與過度活化問題，更為下一代精準腫瘤免疫治療奠定了堅實的基礎。

【研究問題】儘管CAR-T細胞療法在血液腫瘤治療中成效卓著，但許多患者面臨細胞在體內迅速「疲憊」（exhaustion）的困境。傳統上，為了降低副作用，科學家依賴外部藥物來暫時抑制T細胞活性，但這會干擾治療的連續性。如何讓免疫細胞具備「自我感知」與「自我調節」的能力，在過度活躍時自動減少受體數量，而在需要時恢復活力，一直是領域內的巨大挑戰。

【研究方法】研究團隊首先透過大規模篩選，發現T細胞活化後，表面的CD62L蛋白會被ADAM17蛋白酶快速切割並脫落。他們從中提取出一個僅含15個胺基酸的微小序列，將其嵌入到CAR受體中，構建了AIR系統。隨後，他們在多種CAR-T細胞模型（包括針對白血病和骨肉瘤的模型）以及活體小鼠腫瘤模型中進行了嚴謹測試，並結合CRISPR基因編輯技術，將此機制應用於內源性蛋白，以驗證其廣泛的適用性與安全性。

【結果】實驗顯示，AIR系統能根據T細胞活化的程度精確調控受體數量。對於因「基礎訊號過強」而易疲勞的CAR-T細胞，AIR顯著減少了細胞疲勞標記，使它們在腫瘤模型中展現出更強的殺傷力並延長了存活率；對於一般CAR-T細胞，AIR則能有效降低活化引起的細胞死亡，促進細胞擴增。此外，該系統還成功用於編寫「邏輯閘」，讓T細胞只在偵測到特定組合抗原時才展開攻擊，並實現了對內源性受體的自主控制。這標誌著CAR-T療法正邁向更智能、更可控的新紀元。
summary.en:
**Summary:** Researchers from Stanford University published a landmark study in *Cell*, introducing a novel genetic switch called "Activation-Induced Release" (AIR). By harnessing the natural protease ADAM17, this technology empowers immune cells (specifically CAR-T cells) to autonomously regulate their surface receptor density. This breakthrough addresses the critical issue of T-cell exhaustion, paving the way for smarter, more durable cancer immunotherapies.

**Problem:** While CAR-T cell therapy has revolutionized the treatment of blood cancers, a major hurdle remains: T cells often become "exhausted" or dysfunctional within the tumor microenvironment. Currently, scientists rely on external drugs to dampen T-cell activity, but this disrupts the continuous fight against cancer. The scientific community has long sought a way to engineer T cells with "self-awareness"—the ability to automatically reduce receptor expression when overstimulated to prevent burnout, while maintaining potency when needed.

**Approach:** The team conducted a massive screen of the T-cell surfaceome and discovered that the protein CD62L is rapidly shed upon T-cell activation via the enzyme ADAM17. They isolated a tiny 15-amino-acid sequence responsible for this shedding and embedded it into CAR constructs to create the AIR platform. They rigorously tested this system across various CAR-T models, including those targeting leukemia and osteosarcoma, in both in vitro settings and living mouse models. Furthermore, they utilized CRISPR gene-editing to integrate this mechanism into endogenous proteins, demonstrating its versatility beyond just artificial receptors.

**Results:** The AIR system proved highly effective. For CAR-T cells prone to exhaustion due to high "tonic signaling," AIR significantly reduced exhaustion markers and improved tumor clearance and survival in mice. For standard CAR-T cells, AIR minimized activation-induced cell death and enhanced expansion. Crucially, the modularity of AIR allowed researchers to build "logic gates," enabling T cells to target tumors only when specific antigen combinations were present, thereby sparing healthy tissue. This work establishes AIR as a foundational tool for next-generation, self-regulating cell therapies.

keyArticle.title: Cell-autonomous control of CAR signaling and receptor shedding via ADAM17-mediated proteolysis
